thread:
sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's driver+CUDA canary (driver 536 / CUDA 12.2) we started seeing flapping on a subset of Dedicated H100 nodes in eu-west1.
deploy-bot: canary rollout 536 -> eu-west1-h100-pool-1 started at 2026-03-02T09:12Z (artifact: driver-536-cuda12.2)
maria: Symptoms?
sam: Jobs that pin to dedicated pools hitting intermittent NCCL timeout, long stalls while initializing cuBLAS/cuInit, and occasional container OOMs even though memory wasn't exhausted. Logs show `cuInit: unknown error` and repeated `NCCL WARN` lines.
lee: Did you check kernel vs driver ABI? We had a kernel patch landed last week to host kernels in eu-west1; maybe mismatch.
sam: Ran modinfo/nvidia on affected hosts — module reports version 536.11 but dmesg shows "nvidia: failed to register device, error -22" on 3/12 hosts. Non-affected hosts show the same module version but no errors.
devops-oncall: Quick health checks:
- `ssh node-ew1-h100-03 -- dmesg | tail -n 40`
- `nvidia-smi -a`
- `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`

ops-runner: Also saw repeated `peer-to-peer` errors in kernel logs on the same hosts. Could be PCI enumeration timing on particular host BIOS revisions.
maria: Okay, immediate plan? We should avoid broad rollout until root cause.
lee: Agree. Suggest pause the remaining phased rollout and mark current canary as partial failure. We need to decide between rollback to driver-535 or apply host kernel workaround.
sam: We already have customers on Dedicated in eu-west1 — sales flagged two active customers running latency-sensitive workloads. If we rollback we'll pay some orchestration cost but avoid cascades.
nisha: I'll coordinate customer comms if we pause. Can we quantify risk window? How many dedicated pools impacted?
ops-runner: Affected: eu-west1-h100-pool-1 (12 nodes) — 3 nodes showing failures. eu-west1-h100-pool-2 unaffected. Worldwide: no issues in us-west or asia so far.
devops-oncall: Proposed immediate actions:
1) Pause rollout (deploy-bot: pause-targets eu-west1-h100-pool-*)
2) Move new allocations away from pool-1: set pool-1 to cordon in autoscaler
3) Create a remediation canary (2 nodes) with driver-535 (previous stable) and run stress/nccl-tests
4) If stable, rollback pool-1 to driver-535 during maintenance window

sam: For rollback, here's the sequence I suggest:
```
# mark nodes unschedulable
kubectl cordon node-ew1-h100-03
kubectl drain node-ew1-h100-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# install driver-535 package on host
sudo dpkg -i /opt/drivers/nvidia-driver-535_*.deb
reboot
# post-boot checks
nvidia-smi -L && python3 /opt/tests/nccl/allreduce_smoke.py
kubectl uncordon node-ew1-h100-03
```
lee: That looks good. We should also capture kernel module selinux/secureboot failures — some nodes have secureboot enabled; 536 might require signed modules.
maria: Great catch. Check `mokutil --sb-state` on affected hosts.
ops-runner: cost note: keeping the rollback and extra test canaries will keep ~4 nodes out of service for ~2 hours; that's ~8 GPU-hours billed. Larger cost if we need to repro across more nodes.
nisha: I'll draft customer note: short blurb + apology + ETA for full rollback if needed. Also ask CS to surface any running jobs that may be impacted.
deploy-bot: action: rollout paused by @lee at 2026-03-02T09:34Z :white_check_mark:
sam: Tests on driver-535 canary now running on node-ew1-h100-11. Expect results in 20m.
maria: If 535 fixes it we keep it as fallback profile in the model catalog for Dedicated pools until we get kernel-signed 536 builds.
lee: Long term: require host kernel + driver compatibility matrix as a gating step in the rollout pipeline. Also add secureboot flag detection to preflight.
devops-oncall: I'll open an infra ticket with steps and assign to eng-runtime to investigate kernel ABI differences. Ticket: INFRA-2026 (link: https://jira.redwood/INFRA-2026)
ops-runner: Also add a monitoring rule to alert if `cuInit` errors spike > 5/min on any pool during a rollout.
sam: If 535 canary passes, schedule rollback maintenance at 01:00 UTC to minimize customer impact. Otherwise escalate to vendor (NVIDIA) with dmesg and repro logs.
maria: Also we should run a quick inventory of BIOS versions for all H100 hosts in eu-west1 — suspect a subset has older firmware.
lee: Agree. Add firmware versions to ticket.
nisha: I'll prepare customer-facing status message and post to #customer-success and to customers on Dedicated via email template.
sam: OK, locking in actions: pause rollout, run 535 canary, collect logs, if stable rollback pool-1 to 535 in maintenance window, notify customers. Assign owners: sam (tech lead), lee (rollback ops), devops-oncall (monitoring), nisha (customer comms).
maria: One more: notify finance if rollback causes sustained capacity shortfall so we can temporarily spin up replacement capacity in us-west3, cost delta estimate ~ $120/hr if we need burst GPUs.
ops-runner: noted. I'll prepare a quick runbook for the rollback and post here.
sam: Thanks everyone. Keep thread updated with test results. :eyes:
